_note: Game-plan steps, one per question and starting level. Key = question number (1-9). '1' = the step when the answer scored 1 point (adds 4 to reach Strong); '3' = when it scored 3 (adds 2). 'priority' breaks ties between steps that add the same points: lower comes first (safety first).

1: Set nutrition targets for every age group
Agree age-wise targets for energy, protein, fibre and key nutrients with a nutritionist, and plan the next menu cycle from them.
3: Turn balanced menus into targeted ones: set age-wise nutrition targets and check each new menu against them before it goes live.

1: Start with nutrient values for the 10 most-served dishes, checked by a nutritionist and shown on the menu board.
3: Extend nutrient analysis from selected meals to every menu cycle, reviewed by a nutritionist and shared with families.

1: For example: fried snacks no more than twice a week, water as the default drink, and fruit or salad at every meal.
3: Extend your limits to the full menu
Apply your sugar, salt, fried and processed food limits to every meal, with fresh, whole ingredients as the default.

1: Put food safety records in place
Start daily temperature and cleaning logs, train every food handler, and schedule regular kitchen inspections.
3: Schedule regular food safety audits, log every corrective action and keep certifications current.

1: Label allergens and keep a register
Add allergen information to every dish on the menu and keep an up-to-date list of students with allergies at the counter.
3: Add allergen checks at every step
Record allergens for every recipe, separate preparation where needed, train staff, and check at the point of service.

1: Review your food programme on a schedule
Hold a short monthly review of feedback, safety and menu data, and agree one change each time.
3: Bring nutrition, feedback and audit data together, choose one change to test, and measure the result.

1: Run a termly workshop on healthier choices for each age group, and invite parents to one session a year.
3: Add cooking sessions and food exploration for each age group, for example through a Teaching Kitchen.

1: Weigh plate and kitchen waste for a month, share the result with students and staff, and set a first reduction target.
3: Make sustainability part of every decision
Track waste, sourcing and resource use monthly, set targets, and report progress to students and families.

1: Share menus and ask for feedback
Send families a monthly food update and run a three-question feedback survey each term.
3: Put up a monthly "You said, we did" board in the cafeteria and share what changed after each survey.
